content.title: Masters leaderboard: Rory McIlroy, Sam Burns tied at top after first round
content.text: Updated April 9, 2026, 7:58 p.m. ETRory McIlroy and Sam Burns share the lead after finishing the first round of the Masters at 5-under. It is the lowest opening round for McIlroy at the Masters since 2011.McIlroy won the tournament at Augusta National Golf Club in 2025 and could become the first golfer to win the event in back-to-back years since Tiger Woods in 2002. Nick Faldo (1989-90) and Jack Nicklaus (1965-66) are the only other golfers to win the Masters in back-to-back years.Woods, a five-time winner of the event, last won the green jacket in 2019 but will not compete this year. Three-time Masters champ Phil Mickelson will also not be competing. Woods is taking time away following a DUI arrest last month and Phil Mickelson is absent due to family health reasons.Scottie Scheffler, who was considered the favorite to win the tournament in the days leading up to the event, finished the first round tied for sixth at 2-under. He’s one of the most experienced in the field, having won the Masters in 2022 and 2024.USA TODAY Sports provided complete coverage of Thursday's opening round: Masters 2026 leaderboardT1. Rory McIlroy: -5 (F)T1. Sam Burns: -5 (F)T3. Patrick Reed -3 (F)T3. Jason Day -3 (F)T3. Kurt Kitayama -3 (F)T6. Justin Rose: -2 (F)T6. Scottie Scheffler: -2 (F)T6. Shane Lowry: -2 (F)T6. Xander Schauffele: -2 (F)You can get the complete leaderboard and tee times here. Could Rory McIlroy win back-to-back Masters?“Obviously it would be nice” to win again, Rory McIlroy said after his round, but that “certainly wasn't the forefront of my mind when I started 2026.” Justin Rose falls out of thirdJustin Rose entered the 17th hole in a four-way tie for third but dropped down the leaderboard, finishing the round tied for sixth at 2-under on Thursday. Leaderboard remains competitive at the topRory McIlroy and Sam Burns finished the first round with a share of the lead at 5-under 67.There's also a four-way tie for third. Justin Rose remains active at 3-under and playing on the 17th hole. Kurt Kitayama, Jason Day and Patrick Reed all finished at 3-under. Scottie Scheffler is not far removed from the top, sitting in a tie for seventh place at 2-under along with Shane Lowry and Xander Schauffele. Magical Fred Couples Masters round derailed by quadruple bogeyGolf is a cruel game and Fred Couples is its latest victim. After birdies on his first two holes of the first round at the 2026 Masters, and ascending into the top-10 on the leaderboard after making the turn on the back nine, the oldest golfer in the field ran into some water trouble.Couples hit his third shot short on the par 5 15th hole at Augusta National Golf Club and watched the ball trickle into the pond. He then did the same with his initial drop shot attempt, hitting into the water and eventually carding a quadruple bogey nine.Couples followed that up with a double bogey when he hit his tee shot at No. 16 into the water as well. He's now +4 for the tournament suddenly and will have work to do make the weekend on Friday. Collin Morikawa plays through back injuryTwo-time major winner Collin Morikawa is in danger of missing the cut at The Masters after an uneven 2-over 74 in the first round on Thursday. But he was relieved to make it around the course in his first 18 holes of competitive golf since withdrawing after one hole at The Players Championship last month due to a back injury."Toughest round I've ever played," Morikawa told ESPN. "I've never woke up this nervous for any round in my life. I can't get comfortable. I have no pain. It's a trust thing." Fred Couples still has some Masters magic leftThe oldest golfer in the 2026 Masters field just moved into the top 10 on the leaderboard. Fred Couples, 66, just birdied the par 5 13th at Augusta National Golf Club to move to 2-under for the first round. That puts him tied with Xander Schauffele, Shane Lowry, Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas for ninth on the Masters leaderboard. The 1992 Masters champion last made the cut here in 2023, when he became the oldest player to make it to the weekend at The Masters. Rory McIlroy is Masters co-leader after fast startThe defending Masters champion officially carded a 5-under 67 during Thursday's first round, his second-best score for the opening 18 holes at this event. He's tied with Sam Burns atop the Masters leaderboard, despite a poor start driving the ball off the tee. McIlroy nonetheless stayed afloat through those early issues and put together three-straight birdies on the back nine. He just missed out on a birdie at No. 17, or else the round would have been even better. Rory McIlroy charges to top of Masters leaderboardThe reigning Masters champion is already back to creating roars at Augusta National. Rory McIlroy is making a charge on the back nine to close his first round with three-straight birdies. He's moved into a tie with Sam Burns for first place at 5-under. This is maybe more notable considering McIlroy is traditionally known for getting off to slow starts at The Masters. He shot an even par 72 when he won the 2025 Masters. Sam Burns is Masters 2026 leader in the clubhouseBurns just completed his lowest round at the Masters, a 5-under 67, to take a two-shot lead into the clubhouse during Thursday's first round at Augusta National Golf Club. He had an eagle on No. 2 and then used three birdies on the back nine to overtake Patrick Reed and a host of others.Reed bounced his approach shot on the par 5 15th off the green and into the water behind the hole in an attempt to set up another eagle opportunity. He had two eagles to jumpstart his first round. Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler and Xander Schauffle are among the contenders lurking close behind on the leaderboard. Scottie Scheffler gets on the leaderboard with early eagleScottie Scheffler is the headliner of Thursday's afternoon tee times and he announced his presence on the Masters leaderboard quickly with an eagle at No. 2. The world's No. 1 golfer has been getting off to some slow starts on the PGA Tour this season and still entered as the pre-tournament favorite. Perhaps it's a sign he's poised for a third green jacket in five years. Disaster for DeChambeau: Triple bogey on No. 11Bryson DeChambeau was cruising along during his opening round at Augusta with one birdie and one bogey through the first 10 holes. However, he found some serious trouble on the 520-yard par-4 11th.Despite driving in the fairway, DeChambeau missed the green from 191 yards out and was left with a supremely difficult lie in the bunker. He couldn't get out of the sand on his first attempt, then took two more shots to get on the green, missed his putt for double bogey and made a 4-foot comebacker for a 7. Patrick Reed records second eagle on front nineAfter taking the early lead with an eagle 3 on Hole No. 2, Patrick Reed reclaimed the top spot on the leaderboard with another eagle on the 570-yard par-5 eighth.After a perfect drive in the fairway, Reed hit the green in two and converted the eagle putt from long range to move to 5 under for the tournament. Masters TV coverage, where to stream the MastersAll main feed coverage for all four days can also be found on Masters.com and the Masters App. Here's a breakdown of the main broadcast schedule for the 2026 Masters:Prime Video: 1-3 p.m.ESPN/ESPN App: 3-7:30 p.m.Watch the 2026 Masters from Augusta with Fubo Rory McIlroy makes turn at 2 underRory McIlroy, the defending champion, has started his quest at the Masters, aiming for a back-to-back victory. His first round play will be accompanied by Cameron Young, the Players Championship winner, and amateur Mason Howell.FOLLOW RORY MCILROY'S ROUND: He's 2 under par through nine holes Patrick Reed rides eagle into the leadTalk about your hot starts, 2018 Masters champ Patrick Reed surged to the top of the leaderboard after two holes with a birdie-eagle pairing.After carding a birdie the par-4 first hole, Reed found himself just off the green in two on the par-5 second. But he still had a putt ... and he drained it.Patrick Reed is the sixth player in Masters history to start off birdie-eagle in the first round, joining Sam Burns (2023), Sam Bennett (2023), John Schroeder (1983), Jay Haas (1983) and Lew Worsham (1954).Reed is playing in the same group with 2025 Tour Championship winner Tommy Fleetwood, who birdied Nos. 2, 3 and later 4 to tie Reed for the lead at 3 under. When does Bryson DeChambeau tee off?Bryson DeChambeau, Matt Fitzpatrick, and Xander Schauffele started their Masters first round at 10:07 a.m. Gary Player offers advice to Tiger WoodsThe most outspoken of the honorary starters at the 2026 Masters doesn't blame Tiger Woods for taking medication for pain management and sleep deprivation. But Gary Player believes there's an easy solution to Woods' problems."All you got to do is don't drive a car and get a chauffeur," the 90-year-old South African said at a news conference on April 9 after hitting a ceremonial first tee shot with fellow golf legends Jack Nicklaus and Tom Watson to officially begin the 90th edition of The Masters.Player had been asked to offer advice to Woods following his recent DUI arrest, and the three-time Masters winner initially expressed empathy for what Woods endured in recent years due to the injuries and surgeries on his legs and back.− Mark Giannotto Eagles for Sam Burns and Max HomaSam Burns makes this year's first eagle after sinking a putt on the second hole, while Max Homa quickly secures the second eagle with a birdie on the par-5 8th hole following a bogey on the 7th. Shane Lowry off to a good startShane Lowry starts off strong on the 1st hole after tapping in a birdie to go 1 under and move into the top of the leaderboard early in his round.Masters tee times todayNotable tee times. Xander Schauffele (+1400) Bryson DeChambeau says he will play with a 3D-printed club at the MastersBryson DeChambeau is taking an intriguing approach at Augusta National this week, arriving with a self-designed 3D-printed 5-iron as he looks to convert a string of top-10 finishes over the past two years into a first Masters title. The club still requires USGA approval before it can be used in competition, and it remains unclear whether that clearance has been granted ahead of the opening round.When asked why he chose to debut the club at this year’s Masters, DeChambeau said simply: it was finally ready."We'll see where it goes. We'll see where it takes me," DeChambeau told ESPN. "All I could say now is, if I don't put them in the bag, it's my fault now." The 10 LIV Golfers at the 2026 MastersTen LIV golfers are set to participate in this year's Masters, starting on Thursday, April 9. Here is the list:Bryson DeChambeauSergio GarciaTyrrell HattonDustin JohnsonTom McKibbinCarlos OrtizJon RahmCharl SchwartzelCameron SmithBubba Watson Masters weather forecast: Latest updates for Thursday at AugustaThe first day of the Masters is set for perfect spring weather. According to the National Weather Service, patrons can expect conditions that are "Sunny, with a high near 74. Northeast wind 6 to 8 mph."Conditions are expected to remain, if not brighten. There will be temperatures reaching into the mid-80s this weekend with generally sunny skies. Jack Nicklaus hits the ceremonial tee shotJack Nicklaus kicks off the 90th annual Masters Tournament with the ceremonial tee shot. Masters prediction and picksNick Stavas, Golfweek: Robert MacIntyre to winStavas writes, "Augusta National famously sets up really well for lefties (see: Mike Weir, Phil Mickelson, Bubba Watson) and Robert MacIntyre's game is in excellent form entering the Masters, where he's made two cuts in three starts with a high finish of T-12. He seems primed for a major championship breakthrough and I think he'll join the legendary Sandy Lyle as the only Scottish players to slip on the Green Jacket."CBS Sports: Xander SchauffelePatrick McDonald writes, "I've made my bed. It's time to sleep in it. Schauffele was the preseason Masters pick, and despite a slow start to his 2026 season, he remains the selection given his improvement across the Florida Swing. The two-time major champion is striking the ball like he did in 2024 and is starting to see putts drop more consistently. Major championships are his calling card."Cody Williams, FanSided: Ludvig Aberg is a good pickWilliams writes, "It's hard not to like where Ludvig Åberg is trending, especially at The Masters. He's finished in the Top 5 in each of his last three starts on the PGA Tour, including the API and The Players, and has done so with impressive tee-to-green play each time, while also gaining with the putter. Let's also not forget the fact that he's had two starts at Augusta in his career, which resulted in a runner-up as a debutant and then a solo seventh finish a year ago." Masters predictions: Sleeper picks at AugustaUSA TODAY Sports' Jon Hoefling offers up a trio of sleepers plus one intriguing longshot who have the talent to buck the odds and put on a green jacket if things break their way.Tommy Fleetwood (+2200)Fleetwood is someone who often gets glossed over when discussing the best golfers in the world, but he's been consistently good at Augusta the last eight years, finishing in the top-25 in five of those tournaments, including a tie for third place in 2024. He tends to play up at Augusta and is fresh off winning the Tour Championship in 2025.Patrick Reed (+3300)Patrick Reed won the Masters back in 2018, so he knows what it takes to get the green jacket. Of course, his presence on the LIV Tour for the last few years certainly hasn't helped his chances. He might be a little too used to playing in three-day tournaments at this point. However, Reed is different.In the seven Masters Tournaments since his victory, he's finished top-12 or better in five of them, and that includes a top-ten finish in three of his last five Masters appearances. A bet on Reed to finish in the top-20 could pay out massively.Jordan Spieth (+3300)It's been just over 10 years since Spieth won the green jacket at Augusta, and he's been inconsistent ever since. Five years ago, he tied for third. Four years ago, he missed the cut. Three years ago, he tied for fourth. Two years ago, he missed the cut. Last year, he tied for 14th.Sure, the pattern would indicate that he's due for some regression in 2026, but streaks are meant to be broken and Spieth has played in this tournament enough to warrant some confidence that he can still do well. After all, he's finished top-25 in more than half of the events he's played this year. Relaxed Rory McIlroy enters Masters a championMcIlroy was a portrait of carefree and relaxed, which isn’t to say he doesn’t want to win another Masters or that he won’t orchestrate a rare repeat, but the pressure of trying to go back-to-back is nothing like trying to shake the label of being the best active golfer to never win a Masters.He’s off that list now, and onto the career Grand Slam list.“It’s completely different,” McIlroy said of returning to Augusta National as a Masters champion. “I feel so much more relaxed. I know that I'm going to be coming back here for a lot of years, going to enjoy the perks that the champions get here.“It doesn't make me any less motivated to go out there and play well and try to win the tournament, but, yeah, just more relaxed about it all.”USA TODAY Sports' Blake Toppmeyer has more on a relaxed Rory McIlroy. Masters phone ban, a wonderful ideaI’m midway down the first fairway at Augusta National when panic sets in. I slap my front pockets and feel no cell phone in its familiar place against my thigh. My wallet is there, but no phone.So, I slap my back pockets. No phone.This isn’t unusual. At least once per day, I lose my phone, wallet or keys — or, all of the above — around my house. Except, I’m not at my house, and my panic is heightening, and that’s when it hits me.I’m not at my house.I’m standing in the sunshine on the first hole of America’s most famous golf course. My phone isn’t in my pocket, because it’s not allowed to be in my pocket.Exhale. Everything’s good.My phone was safe and secure, sitting on my desk inside the press building...USA TODAY Sports' Blake Toppmeyerhas more on the Masters phone ban.Masters location: Where is Augusta National?The 90th edition of the Masters Tournament will get underway this week, and for the 90th iteration in a row, it will take place at the same golf course in Georgia.Augusta National Golf Club has hosted every Masters Tournament dating back to the first one in 1934. That makes Augusta National (and the Masters) unique among golf majors. No other major tournament – those being the U.S. Open, PGA Championship and British Open – has taken place exclusively at the same golf club. — Jack McKessy How many courses are at Augusta National?Augusta National Golf Club has just two courses (or one-and-a-half, depending on how you look at it). The Masters will take place on the club's iconic 18 holes. Wednesday is a slight departure for the Par 3 competition, which will take place at the nine-hole Par 3 course. How much does it cost to play Augusta National?While there are no green fees for the course, the fact comes with a major caveat. Augusta National is a private club, which means the only way to play is by being a member (or a guest of one), being an employee of the club, or by qualifying for the Masters. You choose which is more feasible. How to become a member at Augusta National Golf Club?If you'd like to land a membership at Augusta National Golf Club, you'd better start networking. There is no application process, with membership an invite-only process. The club has a long history of privacy, and while many reports have listed the total number of members around 300, there is no exact number confirmed by Augusta National.Once you secure the remarkably exclusive invitation, you'd better make sure you can afford to actually accept it. A range of reports over the last 15 years have placed the initiation fee at somewhere between $40,000 and $300,000, while annual dues are estimated to run between $4,000 and $30,000. — USA TODAY has more
